title: Prayer for Deliverance
overview: Psalm 55 is a heartfelt lament by David, expressing deep anguish over betrayal by a close friend and the violence and strife within his community. The psalmist cries out to God for help, describing his inner turmoil and desire to escape his troubles. He contrasts the pain of betrayal by a trusted companion with the comfort of calling upon God, affirming faith in divine justice and protection. This psalm highlights themes of trust in God amid adversity, the pain of personal betrayal, and the hope for God’s intervention. It serves as a powerful example of honest prayer and reliance on God in times of distress, fitting within the Psalter as a model of lament and trust.
structure:
**Verses 1-5: The Plea for God’s Attention.** The psalmist opens by urgently calling on God to hear his prayer and attend to his suffering caused by enemies and internal terror.

**Verses 6-8: The Desire to Escape.** David expresses a longing to flee his troubles, imagining flight like a dove to find rest away from the storm of conflict.

**Verses 9-11: Description of the City’s Violence.** The psalmist describes the pervasive violence, strife, and deceit in the city, emphasizing the social unrest surrounding him.

**Verses 12-15: The Pain of Betrayal.** David reveals the deep wound caused by a close friend’s treachery, contrasting it with the expected hostility of enemies.

**Verses 16-19: Confidence in God’s Deliverance.** Despite his distress, the psalmist commits to calling on God continually, trusting in divine salvation and justice.

**Verses 20-23: The Character of the Betrayer and Divine Justice.** The psalmist condemns the deceitful friend’s duplicity and ends with a call to cast burdens on the Lord, trusting God to bring judgment and sustain the righteous.

keyVerses.text: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the profound pain of betrayal by a close companion, emphasizing that the psalmist’s suffering is intensified because it comes from someone trusted. It underscores the theme of personal betrayal distinct from external enemies.

keyVerses.text: As for me, I will call upon God; and the LORD shall save me.
keyVerses.significance: This verse expresses the psalmist’s unwavering faith and reliance on God for deliverance. It marks a turning point from lament to confident trust in divine salvation.

keyVerses.text: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
keyVerses.significance: This verse provides a key theological principle of trusting God with one’s troubles. It reassures believers that God sustains and stabilizes the righteous amid trials.

keyVerses.text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
keyVerses.significance: This verse vividly describes the deceit and hypocrisy of the betrayer, illustrating the danger of false friendship and the contrast between outward appearance and inner intent.

characters.name: David
characters.description: The psalmist and author, expressing deep anguish over betrayal and social unrest. He is both the sufferer and the faithful supplicant who turns to God for deliverance and justice.

characters.name: The Betrayer
characters.description: A close companion and guide to David who turns against him with deceit and hostility. This figure embodies treachery and broken covenant, intensifying the psalm’s emotional depth.

characters.name: God
characters.description: The divine hearer and deliverer whom David calls upon for help, justice, and sustenance. God is portrayed as the ultimate refuge and judge of the wicked.

themes.description: The psalm centers on the pain caused by a trusted companion’s treachery, highlighting the deep emotional wounds of broken relationships and the difficulty of facing hostility from within one’s own circle.
Despite intense suffering, the psalmist places unwavering trust in God’s ability to save and sustain, emphasizing prayer as a means of refuge and hope.

themes.theme: The Reality of Evil and Deceit
themes.description: The psalm describes the presence of violence, strife, and deceit in the city and in personal relationships, reflecting the fallen human condition and the need for divine justice.
Psalm 55 models honest, raw prayer that includes mourning, fear, and desire for escape, demonstrating that believers can bring all emotions before God.

historicalContext: Psalm 55 is traditionally attributed to King David, likely composed during a time of personal crisis involving betrayal by a close associate, possibly during his reign in Jerusalem around the 10th century BC. The city setting reflects Jerusalem or another urban center marked by political intrigue, violence, and social unrest. The reference to walking to the house of God indicates the centrality of the temple worship in Israelite religious life. The political environment was often unstable, with rival factions and enemies within the community, making betrayal by a trusted companion especially devastating. Understanding the customs of covenant friendship and loyalty helps illuminate the depth of the psalmist’s pain.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes the sovereignty of God in delivering the righteous and executing justice on the wicked. This psalm is seen as a model of faithful lament and trust in God’s providence amid trials and betrayal.

In Jewish interpretation, Psalm 55 is understood as a prayer for protection against enemies and internal strife, highlighting the importance of sincere prayer and reliance on God’s justice in communal and personal conflict.

Evangelicals often focus on the personal relationship with God demonstrated in this psalm, encouraging believers to bring their honest emotions to God in prayer and to trust Him for deliverance from all forms of evil, including betrayal.

application: Bring your deepest pains and betrayals honestly before God in prayer, trusting He hears and sustains you.
Recognize that betrayal by close friends is painful but God is the ultimate refuge and judge.
Cast your burdens on the Lord daily, relying on His strength rather than your own.
Be cautious of deceitful words and maintain integrity in your relationships.
Persist in prayer even when surrounded by violence and strife, knowing God is faithful to save.
Trust that God will bring justice in His timing, even when human circumstances seem unjust.
conclusion: Psalm 55 stands as a timeless expression of human anguish over betrayal and social turmoil, balanced by a steadfast trust in God’s deliverance and justice. It teaches believers that honest lament and persistent prayer are vital in times of distress, and that God is a faithful refuge who sustains the righteous. The psalm’s vivid portrayal of deceit and broken fellowship calls Christians to integrity and reliance on God’s sovereign care. Ultimately, Psalm 55 encourages believers to cast their burdens on the Lord, confident that He will uphold them and bring down the wicked, offering hope and peace amid life’s storms.
